title: {Syn} Karatsuba Multiplies by Doing Less Multiplication
content:
Karatsuba multiplication reduces the number of recursive multiplications needed for large integers. Instead of four half-size products, it uses three plus additions and subtractions.

That tradeoff beats the grade-school method asymptotically and is one of the clearest examples of divide and conquer paying off.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
